title: Scoping and licensing
what: Before contract signature: edition, service tier, modules, user licences, non-production accounts. Every Tier 1 question answered and every decision that changes the quote made.

title: Kickoff and governance
what: Sponsor and sign-off authority, project team capacity, go-live strategy and provisional date, how customisation changes are controlled.

title: Discovery and design
what: Current-state systems, processes, spreadsheets and reports; system-of-record decisions; fit-gap. The interviews happen here.

title: Account foundation
what: Features enabled, fiscal calendar, subsidiaries, base currencies, module list
costOfChange: Severe - several features cannot be disabled at all, or only via NetSuite Support
notes: Enable nothing speculatively. Every feature here should trace to a documented business need. Enable Multi-Location Inventory BEFORE loading items and before the first period you intend to open.

title: Structure
what: Chart of accounts, department, class, location, custom segments, accounting preferences, period locking
costOfChange: High - adding a dimension later cannot retroactively tag history
notes: The most common Excel-to-ERP failure is rebuilding dimension logic inside account names.

title: Master data
what: Items, costing method per item, lot designation, BOMs, vendors, customers, employees, pricing
costOfChange: Mixed - costing method and lot designation are one-way; GL mapping is not
notes: Item load is the single highest-risk migration step. Dry-run it in sandbox more than once.

title: Transaction flows
what: Procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, production, quality disposition, inventory movement
costOfChange: Moderate - process and form changes are recoverable
notes: Configure against the real process from the packet, including the workarounds.

title: Controls
what: Roles and permissions, approval routing, segregation of duties, sign-in (2FA, SSO), close-prep saved searches
notes: Build the close-prep saved searches early. They shorten the first close, not the tenth. Roles must exist before UAT and before integration users (L5).

title: Integrations
what: A/P platform, TMS, subscription platform, marketplaces, EDI, payment processors, everything in SYS-4
costOfChange: Low to moderate - depends on the connector
notes: Decide per system: does it originate transactions in NetSuite, or does NetSuite reconcile to it?

title: Reporting
what: Financial statement layouts, saved searches, dashboards, KPIs, traceability test
costOfChange: Low to rebuild - BUT high if it proves the L1 dimensions were wrong
notes: Build the day-one reports during UAT, not after go-live. They are the real test of L1. Run a mock recall against the system as the traceability acceptance test.

title: Testing
what: Unit, integration and user acceptance testing from real samples; report validation; recall test; trial data loads in sandbox.

title: Training
what: Admin and project-team training, end-user training by role, role guides.

title: Cutover
what: Opening balances, open transactions, inventory, reconciliation, go-live date
costOfChange: Very high - a bad cutover is the most common post-go-live fire drill
notes: Opening balances that do not tie are the single most common post-migration problem.

title: Go-live and hypercare
what: Go / no-go, support model and issue triage for the first weeks, first period close in NetSuite.

title: Operate
what: Period close, twice-yearly releases tested in Release Preview, sandbox refresh cadence, service tier monitoring, renewal.
